Emaar Properties plans to buy out Emaar Development for $3.3 billion — The National
sum: In Dubai, Emaar Properties has approved a plan to buy back the shares of developer Emaar Development that it and its subsidiary EPHL do not yet own, for about 12 billion dirhams ($3.3 billion). After the deal is completed, Emaar Properties plans to delist Emaar Development from the Dubai Financial Market, The National reports.

Emaar Properties offered 15 dirhams for each Emaar Development share not owned by Emaar Properties and EPHL. This represents a 19.4% premium to the closing price of 12.56 dirhams on November 2, the last trading day before the announcement of the board meeting.

Emaar Development has 4 billion ordinary shares. Emaar Properties and its subsidiary EPHL own more than 3.2 billion of them, or nearly 81%. The remaining more than 793.5 million shares are valued at more than 11.9 billion dirhams under the offer. On Thursday, Emaar Development shares fell by about 0.4% to 14.52 dirhams.

In a stock exchange filing, Emaar Properties said the offer was driven by “strategic considerations”. The company said that acquiring the remaining shares would enable it to fully integrate the UAE development business into the group structure and manage and finance it within a unified capital allocation system.

Emaar Development also reported third-quarter profit of 3.5 billion dirhams, nearly 8% higher than a year earlier. Its revenue rose 14% to 8.8 billion dirhams. UAE property sales for the first nine months amounted to 26.2 billion dirhams, while international sales of development projects totalled 8.5 billion dirhams.

Separately, Emaar Properties reported a 5.6% increase in net profit attributable to the company’s owners in the third quarter, to 4.6 billion dirhams. The company’s revenue for the three months to the end of September rose nearly 3% to 13.6 billion dirhams.

sum: Emaar Properties to delist Emaar Development after Dh12 billion buyout approval

Emaar Properties, based in Dubai, intends to remove its construction division from the emirates stock exchange following board approval of a Dh12 billion ($3.3 billion) buyout designed to streamline the group's operations. In a Thursday filing with the Dubai Financial Market, the developer said it will pay Dh15 per share for the stake it does not already hold in Emaar Development.

Emaar Development's ordinary shares total four billion. Emaar Properties and its subsidiary EPHL own over 3.2 billion of these, representing almost 81 per cent. The roughly 793.5 million shares outside their ownership push the total buyout value above Dh11.9 billion.

The price is 19.4 per cent above Emaar Development's Dh12.56 close on November 2, the final trading session before the board meeting was announced. On Thursday, Emaar Development shares ended about 0.4 per cent weaker at Dh14.52.

Emaar Properties, known for constructing the Burj Khalifa, the world's tallest building, described the offer in the filing as motivated by strategic considerations. According to the company, the transaction would place the UAE development business entirely inside the group, enabling management and funding through one capital allocation framework consistent with its disciplined approach to capital allocation and long-term value creation.

The company also stated that purchasing the Emaar Development shares held outside Emaar Properties and EPHL would let it streamline and unify the group's structure while running the domestic development business in a fully integrated manner across the broader group.
Separately on Thursday, Emaar Development posted third-quarter profit of Dh3.5 billion, a yearly gain of almost 8 per cent. Revenue for the quarter climbed 14 per cent to Dh8.8 billion.

UAE domestic stocks jump, led by real estate and banks
sum: Dubai, UAE – The Dubai Financial Market index rose by about 1.8% to the level of 5,932.67 points in early trading, Wednesday. Meanwhile, the Abu Dhabi Securities Market index rose 0.95% to 9,553.41 points.

The gains were supported by strong jumps in real estate and banking stocks, especially Emaar shares. Following Emaar Properties’ announcement of its intention to submit an offer to acquire all of the shares it does not own in Emaar Development.
In the Dubai market, Emaar Properties» shares rose 4% to AED 12.24, and Emaar Development shares rose 5% to AED 14.6.

The company explained in a statement on the Dubai Financial Market that the offer amounts to 15 dirhams in cash per share. It is subject to the required approval from the Emaar Properties Board of Directors.
Emaar Properties’ ownership in Emaar Development currently stands at 79.16%. While all shareholders own the remaining 20.84%.
The number of Emaar Development shares is 4 billion shares. The 20.84% to be acquired constitutes approximately 833.6 million shares.
According to the aforementioned price (15 dirhams per share), the total value of the shares to be acquired amounts to approximately 12.5 billion dirhams.

Emaar launches 194 luxury flats in Lucknow, 3BHKs start at Rs 2.15 crore
sum: The 194-residence development in Gomti Nagar Extension marks the company's second premium high-rise project in Lucknow, following Elite Oasis

Emaar India on Monday launched a new luxury residential project in Lucknow, with prices starting at Rs 2.15 crore, as the Dubai-based real estate group's Indian arm looks to strengthen its presence in the city's premium housing market.

Named Elara, the project is located at Emaar Gomti Greens in Sector 7, Gomti Nagar Extension, near Shaheed Path. The development will comprise a single 35-storey tower offering 194 premium three-bedroom residences.
Elara marks Emaar India's second project in the premium high-rise residential segment in Lucknow, following the launch of Elite Oasis in June 2025 in the same township.
The company said Elite Oasis had received a strong response from homebuyers, prompting it to introduce another premium residential development in the market.
Designed by Ideate Design Studio, Elara is an IGBC pre-certified Gold project. Construction is scheduled for completion by September 2031, according to the company.
The project will offer three configurations of three-bedroom apartments, with select residences positioned to offer views of the Gomti River.

In a first, Indians can book Burj Khalifa, Singapore's Universal Studios tickets via UPI | Here's how to book
sum: Indian tourists visiting Dubai and Singapore can now make online ticket payments using India’s Unified Payments Interface (UPI). The Finance Ministry recently announced that the facility is available for Burj Khalifa and Singapore attractions, including Universal Studios Singapore, Singapore Oceanarium, and Adventure Cove Waterpark.

Citing a Finance Ministry statement, PTI reported that the initiative aims to simplify international travel bookings for Indians by allowing them to use their preferred UPI applications for online payments at these destinations.

UPI payments for online bookings were enabled through partnerships announced by NPCI International Payments Ltd (NIPL) in the UAE on 29 July and in Singapore on 9 September. NIPL is the international arm of the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI).

In the UAE, UPI acceptance has been enabled for ‘At the Top’, Burj Khalifa, in collaboration with NEOPAY and Emaar Entertainment. The statement said it is the first attraction in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) to implement UPI for e-commerce.

In Singapore, UPI payments have been enabled at Resorts World Sentosa through a partnership with payment institution FOMO Pay. The facility covers bookings for major attractions at Resorts World Sentosa, including Universal Studios Singapore, the Singapore Oceanarium and Adventure Cove Waterpark.

Stock markets in the United Arab Emirates extended their losses on Friday as fears of a wider regional conflict weighed on investor sentiment. Dubai's benchmark index fell 1.4% to a more than four-month low, while Abu Dhabi's index declined 1.2%. Real estate stocks, including Emaar Properties and Aldar Properties, recorded losses alongside banking and energy-related shares. The declines followed Houthi strikes in Saudi Arabia that heightened concerns about regional security and energy supply disruptions. Both Dubai and Abu Dhabi indexes also ended the week lower.

Stock markets in the United Arab Emirates fell on Friday, with Dubai recording the sharper decline as losses in banking and real estate shares weighed on the market. Investor sentiment weakened amid fears of a wider regional conflict following Houthi strikes in Saudi Arabia.

Saudi Aramco has reportedly asked employees to evacuate its headquarters in Dhahran and work remotely, according to six people familiar with the matter. The move came a day after an attack on a nearby airport killed two people, adding to concerns about security risks in the region.

Dubai's main index dropped 1.4% to its lowest level in more than four months. Emirates NBD Bank, the emirate's largest lender, fell 3.5%, while blue-chip property developer Emaar Properties declined 2.1%.

sum: Dubai, UAE – Trading was active at the start of the UAE local stocks session, Monday. Supported by leading stocks in the real estate, banking, technology and industry sectors, amid the rise in the Dubai and Abu Dhabi market indices.
The Dubai Financial Market index rose 0.46% to 5,968.39 points. Meanwhile, the Abu Dhabi Securities Market index increased 0.47% to 10,160.41 points.

In the Dubai market, active liquidity was concentrated in the shares of Emaar Properties and Emaar Development. The first rose by about 3.5% to 11.28 dirhams, while the second rose by 1.86% to 13.16 dirhams.
The gains in Emaar shares came after Emaar Properties announced that its board of directors would meet next Wednesday to discuss enhancing shareholder returns. As well as capital allocation.
Emirates NBD shares also rose 0.3% to AED 31.66, and Dubai Islamic Co. rose 0.5% to AED 7.40. While Du shares increased 0.17% to 11.62 dirhams.
In the Abu Dhabi market, Two Point Zero shares rose 1.3% to AED 2.36, and ADNOC Supply shares rose 2.45% to AED 7.52. Space42 shares jumped 6.5% to AED 2.12, supported by liquidity of AED 40 million.
Al Dar shares also rose 1.53% to 7.93 dirhams. Al Sayr Equipment shares rose by 6.97% to 3.53 dirhams.
